The sun is highest in the sky around noon, which is when shadows are shortest. But wait, sometimes shadows can be a bit longer because of the angle of the sun and the time after solar noon.

I think solar noon is when the sun is directly overhead, but depending on the time zone and daylight saving time, solar noon might shift. For example, if it's daylight saving time, solar noon could be around 1:00 PM instead of 12:00 PM. So, the shortest shadow would be a couple of hours after solar noon. If solar noon is around 1:00 PM, then the shadow would be shortest around 3:00 PM or so.
